plugins.name: dev-rules
plugins.description: Gate file edits via a PreToolUse deny + reason that points to the project's coding rule sets (logging conventions; extensible by category) and tells the model to Read them before retrying. Rulesets are organized as `rulesets/<category>/<key>.md`; the hook lists absolute pointer paths (not bodies) in the deny reason so the model Reads the rule files itself, landing them in the transcript as its own tool-result. Per `<category>:<key>` dedup keeps each pointer to once per session.

plugins.name: guard
plugins.description: When a turn ends, guard asks the session to run its router subagent over the response; the router names which audit agents would actually find something in it — unsupported claims, deferrals the repo could answer, explanation the reader cannot follow, unnatural Korean, comments in the source it edited, AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md that drifted from a map into a payload, saved reference docs that filled up with local reasoning — each with a reason, and they run in parallel. It also keeps the session off the network: documentation lookups go to an agent that reports where the document is — already saved, in the repository, or in a knowledge base the project configures — and fetches and saves the primary source only when the network is the only place it lives. One switch per agent, all off until you turn one on; whether a session starts with turn and plan auditing armed is itself a saved setting, armed unless the project says otherwise. A separate `interviewer` agent is not part of that: you talk to it directly in its own transcript before any work starts, and it questions you one at a time — testing what you said rather than guessing the rest — until the request is clear, then researches it and, when you close the interview, leaves one brief on disk for the session to act on. A `handover` skill writes a self-contained session handover before you clear the conversation, and the session `/clear` opens next is offered it: guard carries the file's path across that boundary and the session asks whether to read it. Claude Code and Codex. Requires Python 3.11+.

plugins.name: hindsight
plugins.description: Mine past Claude Code session transcripts to surface recurring agent mistakes and how the user works, accumulating both as durable, project-independent guidance. Review refreshes the analysis from new sessions; report shows the accumulated findings and profile. Claude Code only.
